learn.pulse.p1: Each heartbeat pushes a little more blood into your fingertip. For a moment the fingertip is slightly darker, then lighter again.
learn.pulse.p2: The flash shines through your finger, and the rear camera watches that rhythm of light and dark. Lumen counts the beats and measures the time between them.
learn.pulse.p3: Moving, pressing too hard, and cold fingers all blur the signal. When the signal is not clean, Lumen asks you to retake the reading instead of guessing.
learn.afib.p1: Atrial fibrillation (AFib) is a heart rhythm where the beats come at uneven times. It is often silent, so many people never notice it.
learn.afib.p2: AFib raises the risk of stroke about five-fold. That is why finding it early matters, and why doctors have treatments for it.
learn.afib.p3: When irregular readings repeat within a day, Lumen says "possible AFib". That is a reason to share your report with a doctor, not a diagnosis. Only a doctor can confirm it, usually with an ECG.
learn.afib.p4: One irregular reading is usually just a reason to retake. Sit still, retake, and if it repeats, see a doctor.
learn.rhythm.p1: Lumen measures the time between beats. A steady rhythm has even gaps. An irregular rhythm has gaps that jump around.
learn.rhythm.p2: Several things besides AFib can make the gaps uneven, such as movement, a loose fingertip, and extra beats. Extra beats are common.
learn.rhythm.p3: Lumen cannot tell extra beats from AFib, but a doctor can. If an irregular message repeats, bring your report to a doctor.
learn.stroke.intro: A stroke is an emergency. Learn the signs, and act even if they pass quickly.
learn.stroke.balance: B, Balance: sudden loss of balance or dizziness.
learn.stroke.eyes: E, Eyes: sudden trouble seeing in one or both eyes.
learn.stroke.face: F, Face: one side of the face droops when smiling.
learn.stroke.arm: A, Arm: one arm is weak or numb.
learn.stroke.speech: S, Speech: slurred words or trouble finding them.
learn.stroke.time: T, Time: call 911 right away, and note when the signs began.
learn.diabetes.p1: Over time, diabetes can change blood vessels, and that can change the shape of the pulse wave seen in a fingertip.
learn.diabetes.p2: Lumen can look for a pulse shape that research has linked to diabetes. This is not a diabetes test. Age, cold hands, and some medicines also change the pulse shape.
learn.diabetes.p3: Only a blood test can tell. If Lumen shows this pattern on repeat readings, ask a doctor or clinic for an A1c blood test.
learn.hrv.p1: Heart rate variability (HRV) is how much the time between beats changes from one beat to the next. A healthy heart does not tick like a metronome.
learn.hrv.p2: A higher, steadier HRV usually goes with better recovery from stress, hard exercise, and poor sleep. HRV tends to drop when you are tired or run down.
learn.hrv.p3: HRV is personal. Compare your own readings over weeks, at the same time of day, rather than comparing yourself with other people.
learn.hrv.p4: See "How accurate is Lumen?" in Settings for how well its HRV matches a chest strap.
learn.limits.p1: Lumen watches light change in a fingertip. That is enough for pulse, rhythm, HRV, and breathing rate, but not for everything.
learn.limits.p2: It cannot measure blood pressure, blood oxygen, or artery age, and it cannot tell whether a heart attack is happening.
learn.limits.p3: Chest pain, fainting, or severe shortness of breath need emergency care, not a Lumen reading. Call 911.
learn.limits.p4: Saying plainly what Lumen cannot do is part of being honest about what it can.
learn.doctor.p1: Lumen is a screening prototype. It can suggest a visit, but it never gives a diagnosis.
learn.doctor.p2: Call 911 right away for chest pain, fainting, severe shortness of breath, or stroke signs (BE FAST).
learn.doctor.p3: Book a visit if an irregular-rhythm message repeats on different days, if your resting heart rate stays unusually high or low, or if your heart often races or skips.
learn.doctor.p4: Bring your Lumen report. It lists your readings and how reliable each one was.
learn.doctor.p5: If cost is a worry, use the health-center finder at the bottom of the Learn tab.

widgets.androidStep3: Find Lumen (scroll or search) and tap it to see its widgets.
widgets.androidStep4: Touch and hold the small or medium widget, drag it where you want it, and let go. (On Samsung, tap the widget, then tap Add.)

fix.introGeneric: A clean reading needs a still finger that covers the lens and flash without pressing.
fix.why.pressure: Pressing squeezes blood out of your fingertip, so the pulse disappears.
fix.why.motion: Moving shifts your fingertip on the lens and changes how much light it lets through, which hides the pulse.
fix.why.coverage: Light that leaks around your finger hides the small changes the camera needs to see.
fix.why.coldHands: Cold fingertips often have less blood near the surface, so the pulse signal can be weaker.
fix.try.coverage: Now try: cover the lens and flash together
fix.tipMotion: Rest both elbows on a table and hold the phone still.
fix.tipWarm: Rub your hands together, then wait 30 seconds.
fix.tipWarm2: Then lay your fingertip on the lens and flash, and keep it still.
